sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. Home Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Anil Kumar Awasthi
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.

2. In terms of the FIR, it was alleged that through an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. that the applicant was the brother in law of the victim and had married her sister and they also had two children.

It was also stated that the applicant used to beat his wife and thereafter sister of the informant started staying in her parental home and thereafter the applicant allegedly started promising to marry the victim and on 15.11.2023, the applicant took the victim to Patiala thereafter at Patiala something was administered in her tea and wrong was committed on her and some video was also made.

It was also stated that when the applicant wanted to marry, she was beaten very Raja vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. ... on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140406743/
1 badly and was left in a bleeding condition.

entities.text: Raja vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said application was filed on 17.01.2024 alleging that the applicant had taken the victim on 15.01.2023 to Patiala.
In the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim alleged that the offence had taken place at the home of the victim.
In the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., the victim once again stated that she was taken to Patiala.
The tentative age of the victim as disclosed by her is 20 years.
3. Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer.
4. Considering the age of the victim coupled with the delay in filing the application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. and there being huge variance in the statement, a clear case for bail is made out.
The applicant who is in custody since 03.06.2024 and has criminal history of one case instituted by the sister of the informant, the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

5. Let the applicant Raja be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No. 087 of 2024, under Sections 323, 328, 366, 376 IPC, Police Station Jagatpur, District Raebareli, on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 12.9.2024 Arun  Raja vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. ... on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140406743/
